sourceProperties.name: Apostolhegy

sourceGeometry.geometryOperation: Node true 2D source-segment intersections and polygonize; select the local closed face touching each legal boundary class.
sourceGeometry.faceSelection: The smaller local face bounded by creek, road/junction, southern district boundary and mainland river shoreline; the other face is the complement extending around the district northern/eastern perimeter.

reviewNotes: Legal Gyáli-patak is mapped as Gyáli (1.)-csatorna (way 43001647).

The modern Grassalkovich–Haraszti interchange has unnamed ref=510 approaches. The source ref=510 southbound approach and main Haraszti roadway form the selected road boundary; the mapped highway=primary Grassalkovich centerline crosses the creek about 9 m east of this approach.
This junction interpretation is an explicit approximation; the legal street-corridor edge and source road centerlines may differ.
The mapped mainland shoreline is used at the Duna. The polygon does not include the neighboring Molnár-sziget.
No arbitrary segment closes the ring; every edge lies on a retained road, creek, river shoreline or district boundary segment.

source.method: Literal closed source fill contours from the original July2005KSH PDF page9, including all actual native subpaths and touching micro-triangles. Original decimal PDF vertices are evaluated exactly, then mapped by a three-road-junction EOV similarity and vertexwise EPSG23700→4326. No polygon repair, dropped component, smoothing, buffer, clipping, snapping, missing-edge cap, frame closure or current-name-point fit. Placement remains estimated; one two-control alternative is retained separately. Hódtó is invalid in source and already represented, so it is quarantined rather than repaired or counted again.

sourceProperties.placementUncertainty: Geographic placement is estimated from three interpreted source-boundary road junctions, not surveyed source controls. C2 has historical/current street-name ambiguity. Main fit RMS15.03m is not an accuracy bound; an ambiguous held-out junction differs55.76–74.73m. The control triangle covers only small portions ofBelváros/Tabán; other candidate footprints are extrapolated. Source cartographic generalization, road-centre convention,2005/current change and unknown survey/CRS remain material. Literal current-street-name line checks diverge up to1014m where simplified historical descriptions do not match the whole mapped border under current names; no aliases or source corrections are inferred. Independent source Susán/Újváros rail135 check differs by up to84.21m. These diagnostics do not establish absolute accuracy or whole current extents. Four detached village depictions are schematic/compressed and are retained only in native source coordinates.

source.method: Native625×883 original2014 municipal JPEG color-mask extraction. Manually identified source-colored components use documented HSV classes and4-neighbour connectivity. Small enclosed source-number/CAD-ink mask holes are filled after source review; white exterior/rural gaps and separate components are not bridged. Every native contour edge follows actual classified pixel-cell boundaries; only exactly collinear cell-edge vertices are omitted. Fourteen components retain raster-color estimates of the drawn outline. Two specifically reviewed CAD/digit-occluded silhouettes (northeast8 and northernmost9) instead follow closed8-neighbour cycles of actual dark source pixels (maxRGB165) within3px manually identified outer-stroke corridors; their full RGB/pixel paths are archived. No missing dark-pixel gap is bridged. WGS84 positions use an INFERRED, unvalidated EOV similarity from two assumed source-image/modern-road-node correspondences. Literal modern node coordinates are verified, but no image correspondence or independent physical holdout is established. No hull, image-frame closure, arbitrary closing chord, buffering, repair, current-road boundary substitution or clipping to current municipal limits. Unknown absolute accuracy remains null.

Figure78 contours extend beyond the observed common-image overlap and the original calibration image; their full geographic placement is not independently validated. All output is therefore an explicit inferred geographic candidate; exact source contours are proved separately from placement.

source.method: Original embedded municipal profile-image color-component pixel-cell outer contours. All original components and every external pixel edge retained; only tiny fully enclosed cadastral/JPEG mask voids are interpreted as cartographic ink and filled. Native raw masks and outer outlines both archived. Similarity matching to actual corresponding overview color contours, then an unvalidated inferred overview-to-EOV affine fit against current municipality silhouette, then EPSG:4326. No source-name point controls, buffer, hull, chord, snapping, repair, image-frame closure or clipping. Registration residuals are internal diagnostics and do not establish absolute accuracy.

sourceProperties.method: Source-text road circuit polygonized from actual complete named OSM ways; every output edge is a consecutive original node edge.
reviewNotes: The2017 ITS numbers this circuit as a named subdivision of the Felsőváros macro unit.

The name/footprint relation conflicts with a municipal concept document: the same four-road area is described as a suburban/garden area, while the housing estate is described farther out. It remains a historical planning subdivision, excluded from verified current-neighborhood counts.
The underlying text is a municipal source; this derived geometry is not an official municipal GIS or legal boundary.
Road centerlines and divided carriageways are approximations to broadly stated corridors. Exact parcel-side limits and absolute accuracy remain unknown.
No clipping, buffer, Voronoi, hull, snapping, arbitrary connector or geometry repair is used.

source.method: Manual trace of the observed closed dashed Mária-liget perimeter in the original431×523municipal raster, preserving selected source-pixel vertices. Affine source-pixel→EPSG23700 registration uses three physical road/rail crossings from literal same-PBF ways, then EPSG23700→4326. No place points are fit controls; no Voronoi, hull, parcel clone, parent clone, snapping, buffering, repair or clipping. Placement is LOW-CONFIDENCE and extrapolated south of calibration controls. Raster tracing and conventional dash-gap interpolation are explicit estimates, not native geographic source geometry.
